problems: The blind guess (standing or dancing human with arms out) does not match the intended subject, a seabird with a long beak. Only the lowest-confidence alternative, a stylised bird, is close.
The figure is upright, with the head at top and the foot at bottom, and the beak points left to the tip star. Orientation is correct.
The eye star (around 26176) and the crown-of-head star (26207) sit very close together at the top of the head. Their labels ('crown of the head' and 'eye') overlap each other.
The 'base of the beak' label collides with the eye label, and the 'tip of the beak, holding the sand-eels' label runs through the gold beak line.
The wing-root label is printed over the wingtip label, and the wingtip star (25336) is a bright, isolated dot at the far right. It reads as a detached point rather than the end of a wing.
The 'belly and leg joint' label sits on top of the blue body outline, and the 'base of the tail' and 'outer tail feather' labels crowd each other.
The blue body outlines are real silhouette shapes (head, teardrop body, wing, tail), not copies of the gold lines. The gold lines act as a skeleton overlay, which is acceptable.
The foot star (26885) is isolated at the bottom, and the leg is a thin gold line. The leg is hard to read as a body part.
output.advice: 1) Make the bird read clearly: enlarge the silhouette so the long pointed beak, rounded head, folded wing and forked tail are distinct. 2) Separate the head stars: move the eye (26176) inside the head outline, and keep the crown (26207) on the top edge, so the two labels do not collide. 3) Move the 'base of the beak' label up or to the left, away from the eye. 4) Put the beak-tip label outside the gold line, above or below it. 5) Place the wingtip (25336) at the end of the wing outline, and place the wing-root label (25813) below the wing so it doesn't overlap the wingtip label. 6) Offset the 'belly and leg joint' label off the body outline. 7) Shift the tail labels so the base-of-tail and outer-feather labels don't overlap. 8) Give the foot (26885) a visible leg connecting it to the belly joint (26594) so the leg reads as part of the body."]
